shared_frontend_hardening.behavior_before: success notification was emitted before invalidation and without proving the authoritative read completed
shared_frontend_hardening.behavior_after: the mutation resolves only after the active server-backed collection refetch completes; a committed mutation with failed reconciliation is surfaced distinctly and never reported as success

negative_control_sweep.notes: The centralized React route registry, shared resource executor, action button, dialogs, server-backed search/pagination, loading/error/empty states and capability gates were inspected. No control is promoted to terminal solely because it renders or because this shared hardening applies.

backend_contract_blockers.impact: The frontend cannot bind a visible action contract to the canonical operation ledger, so operation-specific terminal evidence cannot be produced without guessing.

The frontend cannot independently prove that an enabled mutation contract belongs to the active tenant. Backend authorization may still reject misuse, but strict visible-control terminality requires explicit ownership evidence.
Site-scoped visible actions cannot be independently reconciled to the selected site from the frontend contract.

ActionContract.tenant_id: active tenant identifier or other verifiable tenant ownership token
ActionContract.site_id: site identifier when the action is site-scoped

truthfulness_note: Expected parity delta is intentionally not claimed. Re-run canonical reconciliation only after the backend action metadata exists and each control has operation-specific ownership, authorization, authoritative reconciliation and test evidence.
